verdict.rationale: Replicate's own docs say users can improve open-source models with their own data to create new models, and its pricing covers both training public models and serving fine-tunes. Billing for fast-booting fine-tunes is per active request time, which shows the fine-tuned result is served on the same platform. missing for 10: detailed training API/workflow documentation, an explicit list of supported base models beyond the Flux example, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, I can fine-tune a supported base model on my own data and serve the result on the same platform

citations.quote: You can improve open-source models with your own data to create new models that are better suited to specific tasks.
When running or training one of these public models, you only pay for the time it takes to process your request.
For fast booting fine-tunes you'll only be billed for the time the model is active and processing your requests
